theater: 安納托利亞高原與敘利亞

battle.name: 第一次土埃戰爭
battle.theater: 安納托利亞高原與敘利亞
battle.brief: 一八三一年，穆罕默德·阿里索取敘利亞的督轄權被拒，埃及軍西進；一八三二年十二月廿一日康雅之役、隔年六月三十日尼西卜之役，兩度擊潰鄂圖曼主力，迫使蘇丹承認埃及自治。線列燧發槍齊射與集中火砲已決定戰局，長槍方陣退居舊制步兵與守備隊的配角。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 交戰一方是鄂圖曼帝國：安納托利亞、魯梅利亞行省的常備步兵與炮兵為骨幹，另有來自敘利亞、伊拉克的阿拉伯與庫爾德分隊，依附政府的省區民兵（müfetah），以及各門顯貴自帶的私兵。指揮系統以伊斯坦堡的塞拉塞克（大維齊爾）為核心，軍令經安納托利亞、敘利亞、伊拉克三大軍區分線下達；1832年康雅之役由大維齊爾穆赫辛帕夏（Muḥsin Pasha）節制全軍，1833年尼西卜之役改由新任大維齊爾胡塞夫帕夏（Koca Hüsrev Pasha）率領。野戰炮隊多屬舊式中口徑野戰砲，砲車與彈藥靠牛車輸送，給養取自沿途城鎮的徵發，行軍速度受非技術人員比例限制。另一方是穆罕默德·阿里帕夏治下的埃及：核心是按歐洲操典編成的「尼贊」（Nizam，新制）步兵與相應炮兵，由法國、義大利等歐洲教官操練；馬穆魯克與切爾克斯騎兵擔任衝鋒、掩護兩翼與追擊；舊制土軍與受薪傭兵散在兩翼雜用。海軍是1820年代起在亞歷山大港建造的近代帆列陣艦分艦隊，並在阿勒頗、雅法一帶設有陸戰隊與基地。
countriesEn: One side was the Ottoman Empire. The regular infantry and artillery of the Anatolian and Rumelian provinces formed the backbone, joined by Arab and Kurdish detachments from Syria and Iraq, by provincial militias (müfetah) attached to the government, and by the private retainers of the notables. Command ran through the Serasker (Grand Vizier) in Istanbul, with orders distributed along three separate lines, Anatolia, Syria and Iraq: the whole army at the Battle of Konya in 1832 was directed by the Grand Vizier Muhsin Pasha, while by the Battle of Nezib in 1833 the command had passed to the newly appointed Grand Vizier Koca Hüsrev Pasha. The field artillery was largely of the older medium-calibre type, its guns and ammunition hauled by ox carts, and its supplies drawn by requisition from the towns on the march, so the rate of movement was limited by the share of untrained men. The other side was Egypt under Muhammad Ali Pasha. Its core was the Nizam (new-model) infantry and its artillery, drilled to European manuals by French and Italian officers; Mamluk and Circassian cavalry charged, covered the flanks and pursued the broken enemy; old Ottoman-style troops and paid auxiliaries were used in the margins. Its navy was a modern sail-of-the-line squadron built at Alexandria from the 1820s onward, with marines and bases around Aleppo and Jaffa.
people: 穆罕默德·阿里帕夏（Meḥmed Ali）自1805年執政埃及，靠歐洲式軍制、兵工廠與徵兵法重建軍力，1811至1818年先後征伐阿拉伯半島與蘇丹，1820年代又在摩洛哥與希臘用兵；1831年他要求敘利亞與阿勒頗的督轄權，並以協助鎮壓希臘起義、供應軍費為條件向蘇丹索價，遭拒後命長子易卜拉欣帕夏（Ibrāhīm Pasha）出兵。這位被歐洲報紙稱為「埃及征服者」的將領是全場最關鍵的人物：康雅與尼西卜兩役均由他指揮，兵法上以嚴整的射擊紀律、炮兵壟斷與騎兵迂迴取勝。鄂圖曼方面，除前述兩位大維齊爾，真正左右局勢的是穆斯塔法·雷希德帕夏（Mustafa Reşid Pasha），他在君士坦丁堡主持談判，與英國大使斯特拉特福·坎寧、法國大使德·里尼等共同把戰局收束到條約桌。蘇丹馬哈茂德二世同時面對屬國反叛、列強干涉與內部改革壓力，只能在屈辱與讓步之間周旋。
peopleEn: Muhammad Ali Pasha (Meḥmed Ali) had governed Egypt since 1805, rebuilding the army, the arsenals and the recruiting system on European lines. He campaigned in Arabia and the Sudan in 1811 to 1818, and fought in Morocco and Greece during the 1820s. In 1831 he demanded the governorship of Syria and Aleppo, pricing it against his own service in suppressing the Greek revolt and in paying for the war, and was refused; he then ordered his eldest son Ibrahim Pasha (Ibrāhīm Pasha) into the field. The general the European press called the conqueror of Egypt is the decisive figure of the whole war: he commanded at both Konya and Nezib, and won on strict fire discipline, massed artillery and cavalry envelopment. On the Ottoman side, besides the two grand viziers named above, the man who actually shaped the outcome was Mustafa Reşid Pasha, who conducted the negotiations in Constantinople together with the British ambassador Stratford Canning and the French ambassador de Rigny, converting a battlefield result into a settlement at the conference table. Sultan Mahmud II, pressed at once by provincial revolt, by European intervention and by the reformers inside his own palace, could only shuttle between humiliation and concession.
kits: 卡面這件長槍（pike）是十六世紀末、十七世紀初安達魯西亞與尼德蘭步兵的標誌性兵器：硬木長柄約三公尺半，頭端裝鐵矛，尾端留配重，專門用來迎拒馬步衝鋒。西班牙大方陣（tercio）以三個連隊中兩隊持矛、一隊攜火槍交替排列，矛陣在前吸收衝鋒，火槍手在後面成排齊射，這就是卡面所說的「讓火槍隊站在後面」。制度性的變化發生在十八世紀：刺刀裝上燧發槍之後，方陣失去必要性，長槍在歐洲大陸的常備軍中被逐步淘汰，1815年後只餘近衛隊、海軍陸戰隊與少數守備部隊保留少量長槍，用於儀仗與近距離拒止。1831年的鄂圖曼與埃及，「舊制」步兵與省區徵召兵手中仍常見長矛與標槍，這種雜兵兵器在歐洲已近乎絕跡，因此同一件長槍，在安納托利亞的村鎮與關隘仍是尋常裝備，在同期歐洲軍中卻只剩儀式上的殘餘。真正延續下來的是它的戰術記憶：讓火槍隊倚靠能擋住騎兵的正面，站在安全距離後射擊——本場戰爭裡，埃及軍正是靠密集的線列齊射與炮兵壟斷替步槍隊爭到射距，沒有再動用矛陣。
kitsEn: The pike on the card is the emblematic weapon of sixteenth- and seventeenth-century infantry in Andalusia and the Low Countries: a hardwood shaft of about three and a half metres, an iron head, and a weighted butt, made for one purpose, to meet and turn a charge of mounted men. The Spanish tercio interchanged three companies, two of pikemen to one of arquebusiers, so that the pike block absorbed the charge while the musketeers behind it fired in ranks; that is what the card means by letting the musketeers stand behind. The institutional change came in the eighteenth century. Once the bayonet was fixed to the flintlock musket the square was no longer necessary, and pikes were progressively dropped from the standing armies of continental Europe; after 1815 only the guards, the marines and a few garrison units kept a small number, for ceremonial use and close defence. In the Ottoman and Egyptian armies of 1831 spears and javelins were still common in the hands of old-model infantry and provincial levies, a close-complement and missile weapon of irregular troops that had all but vanished in Europe. The same pike was therefore everyday kit in the villages and passes of Anatolia, while in a contemporary European army it was no more than a ceremonial remnant. What truly survived was its tactical memory: letting the musketeers stand behind something that turned a horseman, and fire from a safe distance. In this war it was the dense linear volley and the massed guns of the Egyptian army that bought the musketeers their range; the pike square was never used again.
tactics: 埃及軍的戰術核心是歐洲式線列與射擊紀律：步兵以營、連編隊，進攻前先以散兵與前哨消耗敵軍，再展開成兩列縱隊作齊射，炮兵配合壓制，騎兵只負責掩護兩翼、追擊潰兵與威脅敵軍側背。康雅之役，鄂軍大維齊爾在安納托利亞高原的平原上展開密集縱隊正面推進，但未與敵軍主力接觸即遭側翼炮火與騎兵擾亂，陣腳一亂便全線崩潰，軍官與旗幟相繼被擄，數萬人潰散在高原的冬季道路上。尼西卜之役則相反：鄂軍渡過幼發拉底河後逼近，埃及軍在預先選定的陣地上構築野戰工事固守，把鄂軍放進炮兵射程再以縱隊反擊，縱隊一旦被齊射打散，潰兵在河曲方向被騎兵截斷，大批落伍者與傷兵被俘。補給線是決定性弱點：埃及軍可由海路經亞歷山大港、塞得港與雅法運糧，陸路自開羅經西奈、艾因索爾陸續接濟；鄂軍則靠伊斯坦堡與安納托利亞城鎮的徵發，畜力車隊緩慢，一被游騎切斷，前線即難為繼。
tacticsEn: The core of the Egyptian tactical system was the European linear formation and its fire discipline. Infantry were organised in battalions and companies; before an attack, skirmishers and outposts wore the enemy down, the line then deployed in two-deep columns and fired in volleys, the guns supported the effect, and the cavalry were used only to cover the flanks, chase a broken enemy and threaten the opposing rear. At Konya the Ottoman grand vizier deployed dense columns on the plains of the Anatolian plateau and pushed straight ahead, but before he had even engaged the main body his formations were disturbed by artillery fire from the flank and by the cavalry, the line came apart, officers and standards were taken one after another, and tens of thousands scattered along the winter roads of the plateau. At Nezib the situation was reversed: after crossing the Euphrates the Ottomans closed in, while the Egyptians took up a prepared position with field works and stood fast, drawing the Ottomans into gun range and then counter-attacking in column; once those columns were shattered by the volleys the retreat was cut off by the cavalry around the bend of the river, and large numbers of stragglers and wounded were taken. Supply was the decisive weakness: the Egyptians could bring grain by sea from Alexandria through Port Said and Jaffa, and by land from Cairo across Sinai and through Ain Soukhna, while the Ottomans depended on requisitions from Istanbul and the Anatolian towns; an ox-drawn wagon train moving slowly, once cut by raiding cavalry, left the front without supplies.
data: 時間線可以列得很清楚：1831年埃及軍入敘利亞，1832年夏大馬士革與阿卡先後落入埃及軍之手，1832年12月21日康雅之役開打，1833年5月3日《洪卡爾·伊什凱萊條約》簽訂，5月底鄂軍艦隊在埃及方向投降，6月30日尼西卜之役爆發，說明條約並未真正落地；7月由埃及艦隊護送的鄂軍艦隊駛回君士坦丁堡外海錨泊升起埃及旗，直至協議落實才交回。兵力數字各家記載不一，諸說並存：康雅一役，埃及野戰軍一般在一萬五至兩萬上下，鄂軍約三萬上下；尼西卜一役，埃及軍增至約三萬，鄂軍約四萬上下。損失方面，康雅之役鄂軍陣亡受傷數千、被俘數千人（各書所載不一，以數千之數為較可靠），其餘大潰；尼西卜之役鄂軍陣亡受傷以萬計、被俘上萬人，埃及軍相對損失有限。艦隊方面，埃及分艦隊有主力艦數艘、巡防艦十數艘，鄂軍分艦隊規模相當而訓練較差。穆罕默德·阿里治下的常備軍總數約三萬上下，其中尼贊新制步兵佔相當比重。行軍距離上，埃及軍由阿勒頗翻越陶魯斯山脈、橫穿安納托利亞高原至康雅，行程約八百公里。
dataEn: The chronology is easy to lay out. The Egyptian army entered Syria in 1831; in the summer of 1832 Damascus and Acre fell to the Egyptians in turn; the Battle of Konya was fought on 21 December 1832; the Treaty of Hünkâr İskelesi was signed on 3 May 1833; the Ottoman fleet surrendered towards Egypt at the end of May; the Battle of Nezib was fought on 30 June 1833, which shows the treaty had not truly taken hold; in July the Ottoman squadron, escorted by the Egyptians, returned to the roads of Constantinople and anchored there flying the Egyptian flag, and was handed back only once the agreement was implemented. Strength figures differ from source to source and remain disputed: at Konya the Egyptian field army is generally put at somewhere between fifteen and twenty thousand and the Ottoman army at about thirty thousand; by Nezib the Egyptians had risen to about thirty thousand while the Ottomans numbered around forty thousand. On losses, at Konya the Ottomans had several thousand killed and wounded and a few thousand prisoners taken, the accounts varying and a figure of several thousand being the more reliable, the rest routing away; at Nezib the Ottoman dead and wounded ran into the tens of thousands and more than ten thousand were captured, while the Egyptian losses were comparatively light. In the fleets, the Egyptian squadron had a few ships of the line and a dozen or more frigates, and the Ottoman squadron was of comparable size but less well trained. Muhammad Ali's standing army in Egypt numbered around thirty thousand in all, a substantial share of it Nizam infantry. As for distance, the Egyptian march from Aleppo over the Taurus and across the Anatolian plateau to Konya covered roughly eight hundred kilometres.
cause: 直接起因是穆罕默德·阿里與蘇丹之間的權力交易破裂。1831年，埃及要求以敘利亞與阿勒頗的督轄權作為鎮壓希臘起義、供應軍費的代價；蘇丹既無力支付拖欠已久的貢賦，也擔心讓出一個行省便引發其他屬省的連鎖反叛，遂予拒絕。深層原因是鄂圖曼在1828至1829年俄土戰爭後被《阿德里安堡條約》削弱，希臘在1829至1832年間取得國際承認、1832年《君士坦丁堡條約》更成立希臘王國，帝國的歐洲鄰居第一次集體向蘇丹施壓。穆罕默德·阿里則看準蘇丹無力再打，趁軍制改革完成之際，把敘利亞視為阻擋俄羅斯南下的屏障與安置退伍軍人的去處，趁勢要求擴張。英國與法國各有算盤：英國擔心通往印度的航路與埃及勢力的坐大，法國則因黎凡特的埃及基督徒商貿往來密切而傾向拉攏開羅，於是四方博弈最終變成列強各自支持的兩場戰爭。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the breakdown of a power bargain between Muhammad Ali and the Sultan. In 1831 Egypt demanded the governorship of Syria and Aleppo as the price of suppressing the Greek revolt and of paying for the war; the Sultan, unable either to pay the tribute long overdue or to risk setting a precedent for other provinces, refused. The deeper cause lay in the Ottoman defeat in the Russo-Turkish War of 1828 to 1829 and the Treaty of Adrianople, which weakened the empire, while Greece secured international recognition in 1829 to 1832 and the Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 created the Kingdom of Greece, so that the European neighbours of the empire applied collective pressure to the Sultan for the first time. Muhammad Ali for his part saw that the Sultan could no longer fight, and moved to enlarge Egypt as a barrier against a Russian advance to the south and as a place to settle his veterans. Britain and France each had their own arithmetic: Britain feared for the route to India and for the growth of Egyptian power, while France, tied by long-standing commerce to the Egyptian Christian communities of the Levant, was inclined to court Cairo. The four-way contest therefore turned into two wars fought with the backing of rival great powers.
impact: 這場戰爭把「東方問題」變成歐洲外交的固定議題。第一次大國以艦隊護航、第二次以條約保證的方式干涉鄂圖曼，成為此後半個世紀的先例：英國在1830年代即以顧問身份幫助鄂圖曼重建艦隊，1833年後開造的旗艦級新艦，成為鄂軍新海軍的骨幹。對埃及而言，實際自治的地位由此確立，敘利亞的短期收穫雖然在1839至1841年第二次戰爭中吐還，但世襲總督的位置保住了，埃及由奧斯曼的行省變成準獨立的國家機器，歐洲顧問、兵工廠與徵兵制持續輸入。對鄂圖曼而言，這是帝國在歐洲列強面前第一次被打到要靠外國庇護才能續命，改革派由是更急著推動中央集權、稅制與軍制改革，坦齊馬特運動的動機被推前；各屬省同時看見蘇丹已無力保護自己，阿爾巴尼亞、伊拉克、塞爾維亞的自治要求隨之升溫，帝國內部的裂縫反而加深。
impactEn: This war turned the Eastern Question into a standing item of European diplomacy. For the first time the great powers intervened to shield the Ottoman Empire, first with fleets and gunboats and then through treaty guarantees, a precedent for the following half century: Britain was already helping the Ottomans build a fleet from the 1830s with British advisers, and the ships of the line laid down after 1833 became the backbone of the new Ottoman navy. For Egypt, de facto autonomy dated from this settlement. The short-lived gain of Syria was handed back in the second war of 1839 to 1841, but the hereditary governorship was kept, and Egypt moved from being an Ottoman province to a quasi-independent state, with foreign advisers, arsenals and a conscript system fed in without interruption. For the Ottomans this was the first time the empire had been beaten so badly that it needed foreign protection to survive, which pushed the reformers towards faster centralisation, tax reform and reorganisation of the army, advancing the motive behind the Tanzimat. Every province also saw that the Sultan could no longer protect it, and demands for autonomy in Albania, Iraq and Serbia rose accordingly: the cracks inside the empire deepened rather than closed.
result: 打完的結果由《洪卡爾·伊什凱萊條約》（Hünkâr İskelesi，又譯《翁卡爾·斯凱萊西條約》，1833年5月3日）確定：蘇丹名義上仍是宗主，但承認穆罕默德·阿里為埃及（及的黎波里、希賈茲）的世襲總督，批准埃及佔有敘利亞、阿達納與艾因塔布，另加塞浦路斯與克里特五年代管權；埃及軍撤出安納托利亞，鄂軍艦隊由埃及護送回國，埃及得以維持獨立的財政與軍隊。條約並沒有解決根本矛盾，1839年穆罕默德·阿里再舉兵，列強干涉後的1840年《倫敦公約》把敘利亞歸還鄂圖曼，埃及只保住世襲總督與埃及本土。所以第一次土埃戰爭的贏家與輸家都很清楚：輸家是鄂圖曼的整體權威，贏家是埃及王朝的長遠地位；而康雅與尼西卜兩戰在軍事上示範了歐洲式線列步兵與集中炮兵之優於傳統省區民兵，這條教訓在克里米亞戰爭中鄂軍與英法聯軍並肩作戰時又再被驗證一次。
resultEn: The outcome was settled by the Treaty of Hünkâr İskelesi, also rendered as the Treaty of Unkiar Skelessi, of 3 May 1833. The Sultan remained nominal sovereign, but recognised Muhammad Ali as hereditary governor of Egypt, as well as of Tripoli and the Hejaz, approved the Egyptian occupation of Syria, Adana and Aintab, and granted Cyprus and Crete for five years; the Egyptian army withdrew from Anatolia, the Ottoman fleet was escorted home by the Egyptians, and Egypt kept its own finances and its own army. The treaty settled nothing fundamental. In 1839 Muhammad Ali took up arms again, and after great power intervention the Convention of London of 1840 returned Syria to the Ottomans while leaving Egypt with its hereditary governorship and its own territory. The winners and losers of the first Turco-Egyptian war are therefore plain: the loser was the overall authority of the Ottoman Empire, the winner the long-term position of the Egyptian dynasty. And Konya and Nezib demonstrated, in military terms, the superiority of European linear infantry and concentrated guns over traditional provincial militia, a lesson tested again when the Ottoman new army fought alongside the British and French in the Crimean War.
